review_type: actual pixel inspection of source photographs
scope: Hays County, research-grade iNaturalist grass records
limitations: Contact sheets were made of source-attributed photographs at medium resolution, not dissected vouchers.
Research-grade names can contain mistakes and site/cultivation context is not verified.
None of the eight is confirmed at species level by the necessary minute spikelet characters.
Exact photo-level license/credit controls mandatory before use in public website.

records.visible_in_photos: Tufted dry to green bunchgrass; rather large flattened light tan spikelets on branched stems, with some hand-scaled seedhead views.
records.unverified_features: Detached florets, glume and lemma veins/hair characters not resolved; introduced planting versus established escape not confirmed.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Close scaled mature spikelet, broken florets/lemma nerves and plant basal crown; comparison with other Eragrostis.

records.visible_in_photos: Unbranched ryegrass-like flowering spikes with spikelets edge-on along central rachis; a basal bunch and habitat views.
records.unverified_features: Awn presence/absence, floret and glume dimensions and discrimination from L. multiflorum or their hybrid not confidently resolved.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Paired species views with mm-scale mature spikelets, awn length, basal auricle and glume floret measurements.

records.visible_in_photos: Several fingerlike burgundy-purple racemes and paired spikelets/awn-like projections; strong magnification at hand scale and an exposed collar area in one observation.
records.unverified_features: Distinctive paired-spikelet glumes, exact lemma awns, node collar anatomy and distinction from Dichanthium or KR bluestem unresolved.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Detached sessile/pedicelled spikelet pair with ruler, sheath/ligule and node-hair ring, matched against B. ischaemum and D. aristatum.

records.visible_in_photos: Two to several reddish spreading racemes with awns, some extremely close flowering axis views, a ligule/collar view and bunchgrass basal shoots.
records.unverified_features: The distinguishing pair of sessile and pedicellate spikelets, nerve and awn anatomy versus B. bladhii not measured; species confirmation pending.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Macro of spikelet pair and rachis nodes with mm-scale, compare directly to B. bladhii and D. sericeum.

records.visible_in_photos: Flattened spikelets alternating along an unbranched ryegrass rachis, some clearly awned in close-up; roadside or grassy habitats.
records.unverified_features: Not all specimens' awns, glume characters or hybrid status clear; L. perenne / L. × boucheanum lookalikes possible.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Detailed spikelet glume/awn and basal auricle comparison to L. perenne and the hybrid.

records.visible_in_photos: Some long open or somewhat contracted brome-like panicles and elongated spikelets photographed in lawns and disturbed grassland.
records.unverified_features: Photographs vary markedly in spikelet/panicle habit; diagnostic glume and lemma metrics not shown. One observation has recorded ID disagreement. Current global literature does not clearly support a naturally established Hays population.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Expert determination and Hays voucher/herbarium accession; high-resolution glume/lemma/floret dissection; check against B. catharticus and other Texas Bromus.

records.visible_in_photos: Shaded groundcover with broad lanceolate leaf blades, sprawling stem habit and distinct long-bristled/hooked-looking spikelets in close-up.
records.unverified_features: The precise floret/awn base and bristle count distinguishing Oplismenus species not fully resolved; no plant establishment context vetted.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Macro on same plant showing spikelet pair, awn/barbs, leaf ligule and crawling rooted nodes.

records.visible_in_photos: Small tufted/stolonlike grass and short branched, sometimes crowded panicle with small spikelets; one wet-soil observation.
records.unverified_features: Panicle architecture and glume/lemma hair/awn details do not conclusively separate E. colona from other Echinochloa and lookalike Paniceae.
records.next_diagnostic_check: Macro with scale of mature spikelet, glumes and sterile lemma; leaf collar showing absence of ligule, compare to E. crus-galli / E. walteri.
